description: This bar chart illustrates the average change in compression using two different signal types—“Inferred Frames” and “Lexical Signal”—across various observation probabilities ranging from 0.2 to 0.9, with the horizontal axis labeled “Observation Probability” and the vertical axis labeled “Average Change Using Compression.” The vertical axis uses a linear scale ranging from -3 to 2, with tick marks at regular intervals of 1 unit. Each observation probability value on the horizontal axis corresponds to two adjacent bars: a dark gray bar representing “Inferred Frames” and a light orange bar representing “Lexical Signal.” At observation probability 0.2, the “Inferred Frames” bar has a value of approximately -1.0, while the “Lexical Signal” bar has a value of approximately 0.1. At 0.4, the “Inferred Frames” bar is approximately -2.0 and the “Lexical Signal” bar is approximately 0.9. At 0.5, the “Inferred Frames” bar is approximately -2.5 and the “Lexical Signal” bar reaches its maximum value of approximately 2.0. At 0.7, the “Inferred Frames” bar is approximately -1.5 and the “Lexical Signal” bar is approximately 1.2. At 0.9, the “Inferred Frames” bar is approximately -1.8 and the “Lexical Signal” bar is approximately 1.7. The bars are not sorted by value but are presented in ascending order of observation probability from left to right. There is no visual emphasis or annotation on any specific bar.
